original_question: Find an order-theoretic characterization of Scott well-filtered dcpos, where a dcpo P is Scott well-filtered exactly when its Scott space Sigma P is well-filtered.
target_in_paper: Question 4.5 in Section 4: "Find an order characterization for Scott well-filtered dcpos," together with Definition 4.4(2), which defines a dcpo P to be Scott well-filtered exactly when its Scott space ΣP is well-filtered. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right open problem: it targets Scott well-filtered dcpos, not the broader notion of well-filtered posets, and it matches the paper’s definition that P is Scott well-filtered iff ΣP is well-filtered. It also correctly asks for an order-theoretic characterization rather than a merely topological restatement. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
missing_details: The official formulation is Question 4.5 in Section 4; naming this helps distinguish it from Question 4.3, which asks instead to characterize well-filtered dcpos in the broader sense of admitting some compatible well-filtered topology. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should define the Scott space explicitly as ΣP=(P,σ(P)), where σ(P) is the Scott topology on the dcpo P. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

It should spell out the exact quantifiers in “well-filtered”: for every Scott-open set U⊆P and every filtered family 𝒦 of nonempty compact saturated subsets of ΣP, if ⋂𝒦⊆U, then K⊆U for some K∈𝒦. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The phrase “order-theoretic characterization” should be sharpened to mean necessary and sufficient conditions stated purely in terms of the order on P. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The paper imposes no extra hypotheses such as continuity, quasicontinuity, algebraicity, bounded completeness, distributivity, or Lawson-compactness; those appear only as known sufficient contexts nearby, not as assumptions of Question 4.5. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed purely in terms of the order on a directed complete poset P, for its Scott space ΣP=(P,σ(P)) to be well-filtered; equivalently in the paper’s terminology, characterize exactly those dcpos P that are Scott well-filtered, meaning that for every Scott-open set U⊆P and every filtered family 𝒦 of nonempty compact saturated subsets of ΣP, if ⋂𝒦⊆U, then K⊆U for some K∈𝒦. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: Section 4 introduces the Scott-specific notion in Definition 4.4 and immediately asks Question 4.5 in essentially the same words as your draft. The nearby context matters: Definition 4.1 and Question 4.3 concern the broader notion of a well-filtered poset, so a faithful rewrite must keep the Scott-topology restriction explicit. Section 2 supplies the exact meaning of “well-filtered,” and Section 3 gives the main nearby partial evidence, namely that Theorem 3.1 yields Corollary 3.2: Lawson-compact, hence bounded-complete, dcpos have well-filtered Scott spaces. This shows the intended problem is a full order characterization of Scott well-filtered dcpos, not a broader or differently parameterized variant. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
